title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། གི (Derge Tengyur, vol. 112)
shelf_note: Derge woodblock folio (margin label དབུ་མ་ གི, folio ༢༡) from a Madhyamaka-section text compiling sutra citations (Sāgaramatiparipṛcchā, Brahmadattaparipṛcchā); belongs in the Derge Tengyur.

ocr_errors.image: the line-1 cluster after སེམས་ཅན་ is hard to resolve at this resolution; could be དག་ཡང་ rather than དགའ་བ་ཡང་
ocr_errors.problem: possible misreading in the list of the four means of gathering; not certain from the image

tr_errors_A.english: if one provides joy to sentient beings, or speaks pleasantly, or acts purposefully, or gathers them through consistency of purpose, but does not do so from the state of merely being words up to the point of transformation
tr_errors_A.problem: The source says they do NOT gather beings by giving, pleasant speech, beneficial action or consistency of purpose (སྡུད་པར་མི་བྱེད་པ), and so become merely verbal. A says one DOES all four, then adds an invented condition ('does not do so from the state of merely being words'). The negation moves to the wrong clause and the passage stops making sense.
23,000 koṭis (×10 million) is 230,000 million, not 23,000 million; the number is wrong by a factor of ten
the city name drops རྒྱལ་པོ ('King of Arrays')

tr_errors_A.source: the Brahmadatta verse citation (lines ending in །)

tr_errors_B.english: A monk named Matimant / That Dharma speaker Matimant
tr_errors_B.problem: the monk's name drops དྲན་པ ('mindful', Smṛtimati); 'Matimant' renders only བློ་ཅན

tr_errors_B.english: up to those things which become merely verbal reality
tr_errors_B.problem: the ནས ('... up to', marking an abridged quotation) is rendered stiffly; the quote closes without ever opening on this page

pages.prefer_reason: A reverses the opening sentence on the four means of gathering and gets the number 23,000 koṭis wrong; B keeps the negation, the number and the verse, and its only real slip is shortening the monk's name.

book_verdict: The transcription of this Derge folio matches the print closely. Translation B is faithful and keeps the verse. Translation A reverses the opening sentence about not gathering beings and gets a number wrong.
